items.question: Under what condition must concealment be undertaken in the mortal world among the lowest of men?
premises: Concealment is something that must be done.
Such concealment requires effort to accomplish.
This duty applies in the mortal world among the lowest of men.
items.inference: Concealment is a necessary duty to be carried out with effort in the mortal world among the lowest of men.
items.plain_english: What is to be concealed must be concealed with effort in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

rows.grounds: compound analyzed as given; internal relation between abda and eka+parīkṣita

items.question: To whom and under what test must a previously accomplished object be given?
premises: Something is to be given to a previously accomplished person.
That object must have been tested for one year.
The test of one year qualifies the object for giving.
items.inference: Only an object tested for one year is to be given to one who has been previously accomplished.
items.plain_english: What has been tested for one year is to be given to one who has accomplished it before.

items.question: Which chapter number is assigned to the section that emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: A section emerged from Candradvīpa.
That section is counted as the fifth.
That section is designated a chapter.
items.inference: The chapter that emerged from Candradvīpa is the fifth chapter.
items.plain_english: The fifth chapter is the one that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By whose grace does the speaker come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of the Kaulas.
The speaker has come to know something by grace.
That known thing is the determination of the Kaula doctrine.
items.inference: By the grace of the lord of the Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.
items.plain_english: By your grace, O lord of the Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.

items.question: What is being asked about the soul with regard to both its identity and its nature?
premises: A question is raised as to which soul is declared.
A further question is raised as to what the nature of the soul is.
Both questions concern the same soul.
items.inference: The inquiry seeks to know both which soul is declared and what its nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared? Or what is the nature of the soul?

rows.grounds: locative of ka/interrogative with sandhi as given

items.question: In what does all of that dissolve, and what explanation is requested regarding it?
premises: There is a question of where dissolution occurs.
All of that is said to go to dissolution.
An explanation of all of that is requested.
items.inference: The speaker requests to be told in what all of that dissolves.
items.plain_english: And indeed, in what does it go to dissolution? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What attributes define that which is the supreme reality?
premises: That is designated as the supreme.
That is partless and eternal.
That is free from disease and stainless.
items.inference: That is the supreme, partless, eternal reality, free from disease and stainless.
items.plain_english: He is the supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease and stainless.

items.question: What identity is assigned to the soul that is designated as the supreme haṃsa?
premises: The soul is the supreme one.
That same one is the haṃsa.
That haṃsa is designated as power and individual together.
items.inference: The supreme soul is the haṃsa, designated as śakti-pudgala.
items.plain_english: He is the soul, the supreme one; indeed he is the haṃsa, power and individual.

items.question: Where is the wind-filled air situated?
premises: There is a wind-filled air.
That air is present in all beings.
It remains situated there.
items.inference: The wind-filled air is situated in all beings.
items.plain_english: The wind-filled air is situated in all beings.

items.question: Under what condition is that one called the supreme Śiva?
premises: That one is the subject in question.
The condition is merely leaving the body.
Upon that condition, that one is called the supreme Śiva.
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that one is called the supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: He, upon merely leaving the body, is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: What is heard abiding in the ear, and by what means does it come?
premises: Something abiding in the ear is heard.
That thing comes through tradition in order.
The address is to the goddess.
items.inference: O goddess, what abides in the ear is heard as coming down through the traditional order.
items.plain_english: O goddess, what abides in the ear is heard as coming down through tradition.

items.question: By what means is the result attained, as addressed to the fair-faced one?
premises: Attainment is by this means.
That means is mere knowledge.
That knowledge is what has been heard.
items.inference: By this mere knowledge, which has been heard, attainment is possible, O fair-faced one.
items.plain_english: By this mere knowledge, heard as well, O fair-faced one.

rows.grounds: ablative of ṣaṇmāsa with sandhi as given

items.question: Who should practice for six months, and under what condition regarding the ochre robe?
premises: A person should practice from six months onward.
That person wears the ochre robe.
That ochre robe is free from bondage.
items.inference: One who wears the ochre robe free from bondage should practice for six months.
items.plain_english: One who wears the ochre robe free from bondage should practice for six months.

items.question: What state is attained by one freed from all diseases in relation to yogis?
premises: One becomes freed from all diseases.
That one is with yogis.
That association results in union together.
items.inference: One freed from all diseases attains union together with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, one attains union together with yogis.

items.question: What practice has been told to the addressee, and to whom is it addressed?
premises: This practice of the soul is told.
It is told to you.
The address is to Bhairavī.
items.inference: This practice of the soul has been told to you, O Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: This practice of the soul has been told to you, and to you, O Bhairavī.

items.question: To what kind of person must this be given?
premises: Something is to be given.
It is to be given to one endowed with all states.
It is to be given to one of resolved mind.
items.inference: What is to be given must be given to one endowed with all states and of resolved mind.
items.plain_english: It is to be given to one endowed with all states, to one of resolved mind.

items.question: To whom must the Kaula essence not be given, despite its origin?
premises: The Kaula essence is not to be given.
A restriction applies with regard to yoginīs.
Consideration is given to origin.
items.inference: The Kaula essence is not to be given to yoginīs, even with regard to its origin.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence is not to be given; indeed its origin is among yoginīs.

items.question: In what condition is the speaker's body described today?
premises: Today the speaker's body is under consideration.
The body is pure.
The body has been struck by the veil of ignorance.
items.inference: Today the speaker's pure body has been struck by the veil of ignorance.
items.plain_english: Today my pure body has been struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What does the speaker wish to hear now?
premises: The speaker wishes to hear something now.
That something concerns time.
That something is the auspicious deception of time.
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear of the auspicious deception of time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear of the auspicious deception of time.

rows.grounds: nominative of mṛtyu with sandhi as given

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death?
premises: The speaker tells something.
There is no doubt.
Death is destroyed in the manner stated.
items.inference: The speaker tells how death is destroyed, and there is no doubt about it.
items.plain_english: I tell it; there is no doubt that death is destroyed as stated.

rows.grounds: nominative of sudhī with sandhi as given

items.question: What happens to even the wise one when acting at the tip of nectar with the essence of juice?
premises: Action is at the tip of nectar with the essence of juice.
The one acting is burning.
This applies even to the wise one.
items.inference: Even the wise one, burning, acts at the tip of nectar with the essence of juice.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one, burning, is at the tip of nectar with the essence of juice.

items.question: Where and how should the air be drawn and drunk?
premises: The air is placed at the root of the tongue and palate.
Having made it so, one should drink the air.
This drinking should be done slowly.
items.inference: Having placed the air at the root of the tongue and palate, one should drink it slowly.
items.plain_english: Having placed the air at the root of the tongue and palate, one should drink it slowly.

rows.grounds: accusative of abda+eka with sandhi as given
nominative of yadā+abhyasta with sandhi as given
nominative of jarā+mṛtyu with sandhi as given

items.question: Under what condition are old age and death destroyed?
premises: Practice is carried out for one year.
When that practice has been done, a condition arises.
Under that condition, old age and death are destroyed.
items.inference: When this has been practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: Under what condition does poison not enter the body, even in the case of a bite?
premises: A person may be bitten by great serpents.
Even in that case, poison does not enter the body.
This is stated as a general result.
items.inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
